problem_statement: Kirilbt/interactive-map is a Vite + Three.js Plateforme 10 visitor map: a fixed WebGL campus model fills the viewport, six floating venue markers (MCBA, mudac, Photo Elysee, Arcadia Restaurant, Le Nabi Cafe-Restaurant, Lumen Cafe) sit over the model, and clicking a marker opens a slide-in info panel with schedule and contact data. A native 'Venue wayfinding' control panel was added as an in-flow layer floated over the map: it carries a category filter (All venues / Museums / Cafes & restaurants) with a live 'Showing N of 6' readout, a metric tile row (venue counts and the active filter), and a six-venue directory that reflows and deep-links each venue by its #hash. Three things are broken. (1) The wayfinding panel's metric tile row is a rigid fixed-width, non-wrapping row, so on the 390px mobile map and the 834px tablet map the tiles push the layout wider than the viewport and produce horizontal overflow. (2) On desktop the same rigid row detaches and runs off the panel edge instead of staying inside the panel. (3) The panel is only mounted on the initial map view and never reappears when a visitor deep-links to a venue via its #hash, so the wayfinding control disappears across routes. Repair the wayfinding panel so its tile row wraps and stays legible within the viewport on mobile, tablet, and desktop; so the panel is present consistently on the map and on every venue deep-link route; and so the category filter keeps working (each category updates the 'Showing N of 6' readout and the directory). Keep the WebGL map, the floating markers, and the slide-in info panel intact.
required_content: The Venue wayfinding panel keeps its 'Venue wayfinding' title, the category filter (All venues / Museums / Cafes & restaurants), the live 'Showing N of 6' readout, the metric tile row, and the six-venue directory (MCBA, mudac, Photo Elysee, Arcadia Restaurant, Le Nabi Cafe-Restaurant, Lumen Cafe).
The metric tile row lays out as a flexible, wrapping row so the tiles reflow and stay within the panel and the viewport instead of forcing a rigid fixed-width row wider than the screen.
The 390px mobile map, the 834px tablet map, and the desktop map show the wayfinding panel without horizontal overflow beyond the layout tolerance.

The wayfinding panel is mounted consistently on the initial map view and on every venue deep-link route (for example /#mcba and /#arcadia), never disappearing when a visitor jumps straight to a venue.

Selecting a category filter updates the 'Showing N of 6' readout and the visible directory (for example, choosing Museums shows 'Showing 3 of 6' with the three museums), while the WebGL map and slide-in info panel keep working.
design_constraints: Keep the Plateforme 10 identity: beige (#d6d2ca) map surface, dark-blue (#041676) text, IBM Plex Mono panel typography, white venue tiles, and the sparse Swiss cultural-map styling.
The wayfinding panel must sit as an in-flow control layer floated over the map, never as an opaque overlay that buries the live WebGL model or the slide-in info panel.

Fix the layout and coverage through the panel's own stylesheet (public/hud-row.css) and its wiring script (public/venue-hud.js); do not restructure the map, the markers, the info panel, or the footer markup.
Do not hide the overflow with a blanket container clip that leaves tiles unreachable; the tiles must remain visible and wrap within the viewport.

Preserve the WebGL model, GLB assets, baked textures, floating markers, slide-in panel, schedule/contact tables, Visit website button, and the footer camera controls text (rotate/move/zoom mouse controls).
Preserve the map's own interaction: the WebGL 3D world, its orbit/zoom camera controls, and the marker-click interaction that opens the slide-in info panel must all keep working.
author_notes: Kirilbt interactive-map is a Three.js WebGL 3D world (a Plateforme 10 campus model with orbit/zoom camera controls) whose native product surface is a venue wayfinding directory floated over the map. The graded change touches only the wayfinding panel's stylesheet and wiring; the 3D world, its camera controls, the marker-click interaction, the venue logo SVG assets, and the slide-in info panel are preserved. The panel filters the six-venue directory and updates a live count as the visitor interacts.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial, and mobile_initial capture the WebGL map with the floating markers and the in-flow Venue wayfinding panel; the repair must remove the mobile (390px) and tablet (834px) horizontal overflow the fixed-width metric row creates, and keep the panel legible.
desktop_museums_filter captures the Museums category selected in the wayfinding panel; the readout must update to 'Showing 3 of 6' and the directory must show the three museums.
desktop_mcba_deeplink and desktop_arcadia_deeplink capture direct #hash entry to a venue; the wayfinding panel must remain present and consistent on these routes and render without overflow.
All states must avoid WebGL blank screens, missing local assets, console errors, and network failures.

change_completion: The Venue wayfinding panel retains its title, category filter, live readout, metric tile row, and six-venue directory.
The category filter updates the 'Showing N of 6' readout and the visible directory on every selection.
design_consistency: The wayfinding panel keeps the Plateforme 10 beige/dark-blue IBM Plex Mono identity and reads as an in-flow control floated over the map, not an opaque overlay.
The panel is present consistently on the map view and on every venue deep-link route.
responsive: The metric tile row wraps so the panel stays within the viewport on the 390px mobile and 834px tablet maps.
No horizontal overflow beyond tolerance on mobile, tablet, or desktop.
regression: The WebGL 3D world, its orbit/zoom camera controls, the floating markers, the marker-click slide-in info panel, and the footer camera controls text must be preserved unchanged after the repair.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced, and no existing map, marker, panel, or footer behaviour regresses.
